english: This has been sung in many ways by the ṛṣi (seers), separately by the varied chandas (Vedic hymns), and also by the words of the brahma-sūtra, reasoned and settled. Here brahma-sūtra means the śārīraka (the sūtra text known by that name), the conventional sense of the word, and not any sentence whatever that points to Brahman, since sentences of that kind are already covered by the seers and the hymns, and naming them again would make the verse say nothing.
divergence_note: Read with Jayatīrtha's Prameyadīpikā on Madhva's bhāṣya (their 13.5): Madhva glosses one word: brahma-sūtra means the śārīraka. Jayatīrtha supplies the argument behind that gloss. An opponent, marked in the edition as Śaṅkara, takes brahma-sūtra as 'sentences that indicate Brahman'; Jayatīrtha answers that the words of the ṛṣi (seers) and the chandas (Vedic hymns) are already sentences of that kind, so on that reading the earlier phrases 'by the seers' and the rest would be pointless, and Madhva therefore takes the word in its rūḍhi (conventional sense) as the name of a particular text. This is a textual and interpretive point, not a doctrinal expansion, and neither commentator says anything further on the seers, the hymns, hetumat (reasoned) or viniścita (settled). The contrast is direct: the Advaita rendering takes brahma-sūtra as the Brahman-indicating Upaniṣad sentences, the Bhakti and Advaita-bhakti renderings give that reading first and the sūtra text only as an alternative, while Dvaita, with Viśiṣṭādvaita and Śuddhādvaita, fixes it on the sūtra text and gives a reason for refusing the general sense.
everyday_application: When a word in a document could mean either a general category or one specific named thing, prefer the reading that does not make the rest of the sentence repeat itself. If a contract says compliance is required with 'the regulations, the agency guidance and the standards', reading 'the standards' as 'any document that states rules' would swallow the first two items, so it most likely names one specific standard, and that is the one to go and find.
